intended_object: For a pre-1-hypercover E of S and maps p₁ : W → X_{i₁}, p₂ : W → X_{i₂}, the sieve on W of maps g : Z → W such that (g≫p₁, g≫p₂) factors through some Y_j (j ∈ I₁(i₁,i₂)) via (p₁ j, p₂ j). It is the pullback along (p₁,p₂) of the sieve generated by Y_j → X_{i₁} ×_S X_{i₂}, which appears in the definition of a 1-hypercover (SGA4, Stacks Project). Inferred from the docstring and from how One.lean uses it.
explanation: The arrows field is exactly the condition in the docstring, and downward closure is proved by precomposing the witness h. The definition avoids fibre products, so it works for any category. When p₁ ≫ f i₁ = p₂ ≫ f i₂ and pullbacks exist, the file proves it equals the pullback of the sieve generated on X_{i₁} ×_S X_{i₂} (sieve₁_eq_pullback_sieve₁', sieve₁'_eq_sieve₁). That is the standard second-level covering condition of a 1-hypercover, and OneHypercover uses it in exactly that way. No hypotheses beyond a category and a pre-1-hypercover are used, so it is not too narrow. No other Mathlib declaration defines this sieve; sieve₁' in the same file is the pullback-based variant.
